question: The Mughal Emperor who abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 was:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Akbar**, the third **Mughal Emperor**, is renowned for his policies of **religious tolerance** and administrative innovations that aimed to unify a diverse Indian population.

• In **1564**, he officially abolished the **Jizya tax**, which was a per capita tax levied on non-Muslim subjects, known as **dhimmis**, living under Islamic rule.

• This significant reform was rooted in **Akbar’s** philosophy of **Sulh-i-kul** (universal peace), which sought to provide equal status to all citizens regardless of their religious beliefs.

• The abolition of **Jizya** followed his decision in **1563** to end the **Pilgrimage Tax**, a levy on Hindus visiting holy sites, further consolidating his image as a liberal and secular monarch.

• By removing these financial burdens, **Akbar** secured the loyalty of the **Rajputs** and the broader **Hindu majority**, which was essential for the expansion and stability of the **Mughal Empire**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Humayun**:

• The second **Mughal Emperor** and father of **Akbar**, whose reign was primarily defined by his struggle to reclaim the throne from the **Sur Dynasty**.

• **Jahangir**:

• The fourth **Mughal Emperor** who largely continued his father’s inclusive policies but is most noted for his patronage of **Mughal art** and his memoirs, **Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri**.

• **Shah Jahan**:

• The fifth **Mughal Emperor**, famous for the construction of the **Taj Mahal** and the **Peacock Throne**, though the status of Jizya remained unchanged during his peak years.

• **Aurangzeb**:

• The sixth **Mughal Emperor** who eventually reversed **Akbar’s** policy by re-imposing the **Jizya tax** in **1679**, leading to significant socio-political friction.
